audio_caption: The audio opens with a male speaker asking whether a certain event hastened the death of a different event. The speaker then suggests finding out. Then, music starts to play underneath the speaker’s voice and transitions into becoming the dominant sound. The speaker describes that the email was not a "happy New Year animated gif". The music is upbeat and uses synthesized sounds. Then the speaker discusses the contents of an email from certain people. The speaker continues, mentioning "Strava activity," saying this takes things one step further. Finally, he states that this is a direct plea for elites of the ultra running world to "ditch" a certain event and come together to run a different race.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker asking "And some of you may be asking, why?" in a curious tone, then transitions into a different male voice, questioning, "Oh, have you not heard?" implying surprise and then explaining that it was his "understanding that everyone had heard." The first male speaker returns, explaining "this all started a few years ago" describing the history of the "UTMB points system," and its implications.  He describes how races signed up and paid a fee to offer UTMB points and encourages more runners to participate in local events. This led to more money and publicity, seemingly creating a winning situation, but then he notes that runners were only signing up for races offering UTMB points, potentially harming those that hadn't. This signaled the beginning of UTMB dominating the market.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing the UTMB World Series, noting the shift to "stones" and the "aggressive strategy" of buying races or creating new ones. He mentions the "Gary Robbins Whistler controversy" and invites listeners to click a link for more information. A short sound of crinkling paper follows. The speaker then outlines accusations against UTMB related to the Whistler Alpine Meadows event, stating it's "unsavory" and not well-received in the trail and ultra running community.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing a backlash against UTMB, mentioning their attempts to explain themselves through an open letter and media outreach. The speaker suggests that the incident went viral.

The audio clip begins with speech from one male speaker who sounds like he's delivering news or commentary, reporting that runner Corinne Malcolm was fired by UTMB for being "too outspoken" about UTMB's "aggressive monopolization policy." He notes that this upset many people.

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing "the green runners" and their leader. He speaks in a clear, informative tone, mentioning an environmentalist named Damian Hall. He states they've been at the forefront of growing calls for UTMB to ditch their headline sponsor, "Dacia," which he describes as a company known for making revenue from non-environmentally friendly products.

The clip starts with a male speaker introducing an interesting fact: Killian had been registered to run UTMB in 2023, but pulled out after UTMB announced a headline sponsor. The speaker adopts an inquisitive tone, highlighting that Killian cited injury as the reason for withdrawing and states that UTMB had been a sponsor long before that. There is a mention of UTMB on a banner in a 2022 race video, with Killian winning that year. The clip is delivered in an informative tone.

The clip begins with a man speaking about an announcement of a "World Trail Majors series." He sets it up as a response to trail and ultra-running trends, emphasizing it's an effort to "redress the balance somewhat." Transitioning in speech he references an email. He urges viewers to subscribe to the channel. He then returns to highlighting details for the listeners. During the narration, background ambient noise occurs. Finally, a sound effect occurs.

The audio begins with a male speaker who is suggesting a commitment to race each other "at a race other than UTMB this year." He sounds friendly and conversational. He acknowledges that "UTMB has truly become the main event of the year" and has "really helped put our sport on the map."

The clip begins with a female speaker reading, her tone fairly neutral but with some inflection. She quotes a statement about UTMB, saying they feel the organization is not "managing themselves or their events in a way that has the best interests of the sport and its people in mind." She goes on to quote, "what can we do to benefit the sport of trail running as a whole." She states, "the answer...is for elite athletes to use their influence." Background music that sounds ambient and uplifting is playing under her speech, and it remains constant throughout.

The clip begins with a single male speaker with a formal, somewhat urgent tone, discussing "absence of the top 15 ranked male and female athletes" in the UTMB, suggesting "an alternative race in mind." He mentions "Killian and Zach" and asks about "the Quebec Trail or the South Africa Cape Town Ultra Trail." The speaker finishes reading an email, emphasizing the need to "apply some pressure to the UTMB Iron Man organization" to "effect positive change." The speaker hopes that "we could one day go to UTMB and feel good about it." A shuffling sound is heard, followed by a sound similar to a cough.

The audio clip begins with speech from a single male speaker posing a question about the implications of recent events, asking if it means the end of UTMB and if top athletes will leave to race elsewhere. He then expresses his opinion that it is unlikely and that some elites will seek to win UTMB and continues by stating that sponsors influence athletes and pay for their lifestyle as full-time ultra runners. The speech occurs in a serious and inquisitive tone. In the background there's gentle music playing throughout the clip.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing how sponsors influence athletes' race choices and expressing uncertainty about a mass exodus from a race. He mentions that some feel this is posturing and an unwarranted campaign of hate. He then admits to being unsure about it all. There is no music or background noise audible.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker expressing a positive view towards big business, stating that he has "no problem with big business," and businesses expanding and making money. He believes a particular entity is not a threat to local running as independent companies and races will always exist, affirming his intention to participate in both types of events. However, the speaker also feels that this entity at times acts without consideration for the trail running community and other businesses. During the speech, there's a subtle background music which gives off an atmospheric mood.

The clip begins with a female speaker discussing the need for more transparency and consideration from UTMB, warning that discontented voices may grow louder, as nothing lasts forever. This concern is briefly echoed by another speaker stating that "all things come to an end." The first speaker then encourages listeners to learn more about the Gary Robbins Whistler controversy by clicking a link. She concludes by expressing gratitude to viewers, inviting them to subscribe, and wishing to meet them on the starting line. Light, rhythmic music plays in the background throughout the speech, enhancing the listening experience without obscuring the voice.
